team.name: Bryan Bender
team.title: Partner & Managing Director
bio_paragraphs: Nothing beats hard work.

January 18th, 2008 was my first day working in Commercial Real Estate. I still remember arriving early that morning, and receiving a phone call from my father. “Never change who you are” he said, knowing how nervous I was in trying to follow my brother, Robert, into Investment property sales at Marcus & Millichap. I had to make this work, I cannot fail, I thought to myself. After a one and a half decades of ups and downs, listings and closings, and seemingly endless negotiations, a lesson I learned many years prior while working on a local farm during high school and college summers, still rings true: nothing beats hard work.

My nearly $3 Billion in Net Leased Property sales is a testament to that hard work, but equally a testament to the amazing client relationships I have created along the way. I knew from the beginning that the key to success is one’s long-term client relationships. I am extremely grateful and appreciative for the clients that I am lucky to have, as many now have become true friends. Assisting my brother, Robert Bender, and his partner, Doug Passon, in 2009 we built Fortis Net Lease to better serve our clients in every aspect of the real estate holding / selling continuum. Our focus since our inception has been aimed towards achieving our client’s real estate goals, while helping them preserve and create wealth. Thereby, our goals are our client’s goals.

From FNL Agent #1 to Partner & Managing Director, my wife, Isabel, has been by my side since we met while attending the University of Michigan. When I am not behind my computer screens piecing together transactions, you’ll find me with Isabel and my three wonderful children, either near home or on the shores of Lake Huron enjoying Pure Michigan. I credit any success I have attained to my parents, from whom I learned the meaning of work; to my older brother Rob, for being not only my mentor but also for providing me this opportunity, and to my incredible Junior Partners, Ben and Andy, as they truly keep me on the tracks.
My plan is to continue to work tirelessly for the benefit of my clients, while helping to navigate the direction of Fortis Net Lease and our amazing agents for many years to come.

team.name: Robert Bender
team.title: Managing Partner
bio_paragraphs: One of the first things I learned in my professional career, which is arguably one of the most important life lessons of all, is to do what you say you are going to do. If you follow through with the commitments you make to your family, friends and clients then success with all is virtually guaranteed. Today, as the oldest of four brothers, the father of four wonderful children and as one of the founders of Fortis Net Lease, this very simple life lesson guides everything I do.

I was recruited by Marcus & Millichap right out of the University of Michigan nearly 20 years ago and have never looked back. As a young man, and in my first years as an advisor and broker I was lucky enough to identify the net lease and retail sector as one in which lent itself well to the new “style” of real estate brokerage. The internet was changing the way everything worked! I knew that in order to have long term success one would have to blend the old and new ways of doing business.

Having earned numerous, national sales awards in my earliest years at the largest investment brokerage house in the nation I was blessed with an unexpected level of success. The lessons I learned from those early days and a strong commitment to doing what I said I would do has led me to where I am today.

In 2009, during the worst financial crisis in a generation, Doug Passon, my brother, Bryan Bender and I decided to change the way we assisted our clients in meeting their investment goals. How? By taking a risk, leaving a very comfortable nest and starting a new brokerage company that put our client’s needs first, before ours and before the company’s. “Clients first” has been and will always be our mantra.

Five billion dollars in investment sales later, I attribute hard work, commitment, focus and incredible support from the wonderful team here at Fortis not to my success but to our success and the success of our many, many repeat clients.

listings_legacy_wordpress.description_after_highlights: INVESTMENT SUMMARY Fortis Net Lease is pleased to present this brand new Lazy DOG restaurant and bar located at 1851 Central Expressway N, Allen, Texas. At the close of escrow, the tenant, Lazy Dog Corporate, will sign a brand new 20 year Absolute NNN lease requiring zero landlord responsibilities. The lease also features 10% increases every 5 years to hedge against inflation. These rent escalations are also included in the two, five year options. This is an opportunity for an investor to purchase a trophy asset with a long term lease and no landlord responsibilities. LOCATION SUMMARY Allen is a city in Collin County, Texas, United States, a northern suburb of Dallas. As of the 2010 United States Census, the city had a total population of 84,246. The Allen area was previously home to the Caddo, Comanche, and other indigenous peoples. The first immigrants from the United States and Europe arrived in the early 1840s. The town was established by the Houston and Central Texas Railroad and named in 1872 for Ebenezer Allen, a state politician and railroad promoter. The railroad allowed sale of crops across the country before they rotted, causing a shift from the previous cattle-based agriculture. On February 22, 1878, a gang led by Sam Bass committed in Allen what is said to be Texas's first train robbery. From 1908 through 1948, Allen was a stop along the Texas Traction Company's interurban line from Denison to Dallas. Allen was a small town of a few hundred residents when it was incorporated in 1953. Since this time, it has grown dramatically due to the construction of U.S. Route 75, the Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, and the development of nearby Dallas and Plano. Among the more recent developments is the Waterford Parks neighborhood.
